text.p: Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said on Saturday that President Jacques Chirac had "pulled off a formidable breakthrough" in his tour of the Middle East.

"He gave a fresh impulse to France's presence and created a new momentum for peace," de Charette told the Journal du Dimanche in an interview to be published on Sunday. "This is a tour whose historical dimension will increasingly appear in the coming weeks."

Chirac returned home on Saturday after visiting Syria, Israel, Palestinian territories, Jordan, Lebanon and Egypt. Welcomed as a hero in Arab countries he met scepticism in Israel that Europe could join in the U.S. peace efforts.

De Charette played down a highly-publicised incident in which Chirac jostled with overzealous Israeli security in Arab East Jerusalem, and sought to appease any misgivings in Israel by insisting on France's friendship with the Jewish state.

"France has clearly been a friend of Israel since it was created. We have always marked that our priority concern was for the security of the state and population of Israel. There cannot be any doubt on this," he said.
"There cannot be any disagreement between two friendly governments. It is very important that this message of friendship to be heard in Israel," he added.
De Charette said he would brief European Union colleagues on the trip at their Monday meeting in Luxembourg, and Chirac has already written to the EU leaders about his tour.

He blamed on "an old Franco-British envy" criticism of Chirac's trip by British Foreign Minister Malcolm Rifkind, saying no-one could dispute that France had a role to play in the Middle East where it had been present for centuries.
He repeated that the EU, as the main contributor of aid to Palestinians must play a role in the peace process.
"Europe cannot accept that it is to pay without taking part," he said.
